calls.head: Bobrovsky’s hold on the Senators won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Bobrovsky has been a wall against the Senators, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Senators finally get to him.

calls.head: Penalties could cost the Maple Leafs
calls.body: The Maple Leafs’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Senators’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Maple Leafs tonight.

calls.head: The Senators lock it down, the Maple Leafs don’t
calls.body: The Senators keep shots away, but the Maple Leafs give up plenty. Ottawa is one of the league’s best for shot suppression, and Toronto is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Maple Leafs to give up the bigger pile of shots.

surprises.head: Ottawa got the good looks
surprises.body: Ottawa’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 11.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 800 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Toronto flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Toronto gets outshot more than almost anyone, and Ottawa allows fewer shots than almost anyone. Not tonight: Toronto took 50 of the 81 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Toronto would expect about 42%. A team strays this far about once every 175 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.
surprises.flipped: The Senators lock it down, the Maple Leafs don’t

story.head: The Senators beat the Maple Leafs
paras: Thomas Chabot struck first for the Senators late in the first. Auston Matthews made it 1-1 early in the second, with William Nylander picking up his 400th NHL assist on the assist. Kirill Marchenko scored his first goal for Toronto on the power play midway through the second to put the Maple Leafs ahead 2-1. Michael Amadio made it 2-2 later in the period. Stephen Halliday put the Sens ahead for good midway through the third.

The Senators drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Linus Ullmark made 27 saves for the Senators, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 26 of 29. The Senators improved to 1-0-0, and the Maple Leafs fell to 1-2-0.
